verdict.rationale: Both stop the relay on a bad config, collect every problem, reject unknown keys and missing files, and document the change. B keeps the existing case-insensitive boolean parsing, whereas A now rejects values like `TRUE` that used to work, which could break configs already in production. B also makes `Main` testable and adds an end-to-end test proving a bad config exits non-zero and relays nothing. A's extra overflow check on the timeout and its narrower scope do not quite outweigh this.
a_issues: `metrics.enabled` now accepts only lowercase `true`/`false`, so existing `TRUE`/`True` values that `Boolean.parseBoolean` used to accept will now block startup.
No test covers `Main`'s exit path; the `System.exit` call and the stderr message are only checked by hand.
`System.exit` sits inside `main` with no seam for testing.
b_issues: Adds a new rule rejecting `request.timeout=0s` that the README does not require (disclosed, but still scope creep).

Does not reject timeouts too large for `toMillis` (e.g. `9223372036854775807s`); this passes validation and then throws an `ArithmeticException` in `ConsoleUplink` at send time, outside the `IOException` retry handling.
Exit status 2 is less conventional than `EX_CONFIG` (78) for configuration errors.
Adds a problems list to `ConfigException` and refactors `Main`, a little more structure than strictly needed.

verdict.rationale: Both changes turn silent fallbacks into collected, reported errors, reject unknown keys and fail on a missing file, so they solve the task equally well at the core. A keeps the original case-insensitive boolean parsing, so `TRUE` still works, and it accepts `HTTPS` schemes. It also adds a testable `Main.run` with a test showing that a bad config exits with an error and relays nothing. B rejects booleans like `True` that used to be accepted, which could break existing configs, and it has no test of the startup path. B is better at rejecting timeouts whose milliseconds overflow, which A misses.
a_issues: Accepts timeouts like 9223372036854775807s whose toMillis() overflows; ConsoleUplink would then throw at send time.
Adds a new rule rejecting 0s timeouts that the README does not state (it is disclosed in the report).
The example output in the report mixes a misspelled-key error and a bad-value error in a way that looks made up.
b_issues: Booleans are now case-sensitive, so `TRUE`/`True` (previously accepted by Boolean.parseBoolean) now fail startup.
The URL scheme check is case-sensitive, so `HTTPS://...` is rejected.
No test covers Main's catch, message and exit code; the System.exit path is untestable as written.
